Author: Samit Gopal
Bench: Samit Gopal
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:142744
Court No. - 69
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 22644 of 2019
Applicant :- Naresh
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Som Veer,Kartikeya Bhargava,Satya Priya Mishra,Kartikey A Bharg
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Manoj Kumar Tripathi,Mayank,Vinod Kumar Tirpathi,Maya
Hon'ble Samit Gopal,J.

sentences.text: List revised.

2. Heard Shri Swapnil Sinha, Advocate holding brief of Shri Kartikeya Bhargava, learned counsel for the applicant and Shri Ajay Singh, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material on records.
Shri Manoj Kumar Tripathi, Shri Mayank and Shri Vinod Kumar Tirpathi, learned counsel for the first informant are not present.

3. This bail application under Section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure has been filed by the applicant- Naresh, seeking enlargement on bail during trial in connection with Case Crime No. 1427 of 2018, under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506, 302, 120-B I.P.C., registered at Police Station Kotwali,
District Mathura.

1 4.

The first information report of the present case was lodged on 14.12.2018 by Smt. Madhu against the applicant and six others alleging therein that her daughter Smt. Lata was married with Naresh on 1.12.2010.
In the marriage, gifts and dowry were given, but, the in-laws of her daughter were not happy with it and used to assault and torture her for extra dowry.
There was demand of Rs.4,00,000/- and a car as dowry.
Her daughter showed inability to fulfill the same.
They used to keep her hungry and threatened to eliminate her.

On 13.12.2018 at about 10:00 P.M. accused persons assaulted her daughter and Naresh sprinkled kerosene on her after which Rajesh friend of Naresh ignited her due to which she received serious injuries.
The neighbours told her about this incident.
She then reached Nayati Hospital, Mathura, where her daughter told her of the incident.
Condition of her daughter is serious.

The first information report was lodged under Sections 498A,
323, 504, 506, 307 I.P.C. and 3/4 D.P. Act.
5.
Learned counsel for the applicant has argued that applicant although is the husband of the deceased, but, he has been falsely implicated in the present case.

It is argued that deceased committed suicide and died and in the same event, he has also received burn injuries for which he was medically examined and was found to have received three superficial burn injuries.
It is argued that the medical examination of the applicant was done on 16.12.2018 where doctor opined thermal burn present on his body.

It is argued that the present incident is totally false and incorrect as stated by the prosecution inasmuch as the deceased, Smt. Lata, and her younger sister Mamta were married in the same house and thus demand of dowry only from one sister is very unnatural.

It is argued that there is an alleged dying declaration said to have been recorded by one Vikas Tomar,
Sub Inspector of Delhi Police on 17.12.2018 which is said to have been handed over to the Investigating Officer on 25.12.2018 in its hard form and also in a CD of recording of the same but there is no explanation coming forth in the prosecution story as to where the same remained for about seven days i.e. from 17.12.2018 to 25.12.2018 and as such the chances of tampering and its falsity cannot be ruled out.

It is argued that although the first informant had previously filed a Transfer Petition (Criminal) No. 554 of 2019 (Smt. Madhu vs. State of U.P. and others) before the Apex Court in which vide order dated 4.11.2019, further proceedings of the trial of the present case were directed to remain stayed, copy of the said order has been placed before the Court which is annexure SA-2 to the supplementary affidavit dated 1.2.2021, but, the said transfer petition was got dismissed as withdrawn by the applicant therein and the same was dismissed as such vide order dated 25.07.2022, copy of the said order has also been placed before this Court which is annexure SA-1 to the fourth supplementary affidavit dated 18.10.2022.
It is argued that as such trial of the applicant remained pending from 4.11.2019 upto 25.07.2022 because of the first informant due to the interim order passed by the Apex Court.

It is argued that the applicant is not at fault for the same, he is in jail since 14.12.2018 and in the trial as many as two witnesses have been examined after the same has started after dismissal of the transfer petition.
Further, it is argued that the deceased and the applicant from the wedlock have two children, but, the said two children have not been interrogated during investigation.

While placing paragraph-11 of the supplementary affidavit dated 11.10.2020, learned counsel has argued that the Investigating Officer in parcha No. 4 on 25.12.2018 has noted that the dying declaration of the deceased Smt. Lata was recorded by Sub Inspector Vikas Tomar and he has also got it recorded through videography.
It is argued that even in spite of the same, the said Sub Inspector Vikas Tomar has not been interrogated and has neither been made witness, as such, bail of the applicant be allowed.

Naresh vs State Of U.P. on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126696202/
2 6.
Per contra, learned counsel for the State vehemently opposed the prayer for bail and argued that the deceased died because of extensive burn injuries.

There is a dying declaration of the deceased in which she has stated specifically of the applicant igniting her and troubling her since the last two days after which he committed the said incident while being alone.
It is argued that as such implication of the applicant is there in the matter.

Further, it is argued that there is no such noting in parcha No. 4 that Sub Inspector Vikas Tomar recorded the said dying declaration, the pleading to the said effect is incorrect as narrated in paragraph-11 of the supplementary affidavit.

It is argued that since applicant is the husband of the deceased; he is named in the first information report and also in the dying declaration of the deceased; marriage of the applicant with the deceased was solemnized on 1.12.2010 and the incident in question is of 13.12.2018 in the matrimonial house of the deceased, the bail application be rejected.
7. After having heard the learned counsel for the parties and perusing the record, it is evident that applicant is the husband of the deceased.
The deceased died due to extensive burn injuries in her matrimonial house.
There is a dying declaration of the deceased wherein applicant is assigned the main and specific role of burning the deceased.
Even as per first information report there is oral dying declaration of the deceased given to her mother Smt. Madhu who is the first informant.
Insofar as the injuries of the applicant are concerned, although the doctor found three superficial burn injuries on his body but opined nature of the same to be simple.
The same were also opined to be around about 2-3 days old.

The other argument with regard to the children of the deceased and the applicant not being interrogated during investigation and with regard to the veracity of the dying declaration, the same is matter of trial.

Insofar as the delay in trial is concerned, the same cannot be a ground for release of the applicant as trial was stayed by the Apex Court in a transfer petition which was subsequently dismissed as withdrawn after which as per statement of learned counsel for the applicant, two witnesses have been examined.
7. Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, I do not find it a fit case for bail, hence, the bail application is rejected.

Order Date :- 18.7.2023 Mukesh Kr.
(Samit Gopal,J.)
